newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed in negative territory as a wave of profit-taking snuffed out an afternoon rally triggered by a new batch of U.S. economic data.
Dutch and German bonds had opened lower but later rallied with U.S. Treasuries on U.S. producer price and retail sales data which helped to allay inflationary fears.
But while Treasuries remained strong, the rally was taken as a cue for profit-taking in bunds and Dutch bonds duly followed.
The benchmark Jan 2006 issue closed 15 cents lower at 100.55/63 for a yield of 5.91 percent -- a steady 12 basis points below the yield on the April 2006 bund.
Dutch September CPI data showing a year-on-year inflation rate of 2.0 percent, versus 1.4 percent in Germany, was in line with expectations and had no impact on bond prices.
Dealers said the inflation gap meant little to the bond market as extremely tight supply would continue to keep Dutch yields below those in Germany all along the curve.
Foreigners had recently shown scant interest in the Dutch bond market, preferring EMU convergence plays in the "Club Med" countries of southern Europe, they added.
